newsitem.title: IRAN: NIOC TO CUT SPOT CRUDE SALES WITH NEW REFINERY.
newsitem.headline: NIOC TO CUT SPOT CRUDE SALES WITH NEW REFINERY.

text.p: National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC) will cut spot crude sales as the new Bandar Abbas refinery gears up for operations and absorbs more Iranian oil output, Vice Petroleum Minister Ghanimi Fard said on Thursday.
"The production that we are having now in the Bandar Abbas refinery we are decreasing from the spot market," Fard told Reuters.
"Proportionately it (spot sales) is going to be decreased...this is going to be the priority."
NIOC sells around 10 percent of its total crude exports of 2.5 million barrels per day (bpd) on a spot basis to traders, refiners and other end-users.
These spot sales are widely used by NIOC and the oil market to gauge the value of Iranian crude.
Supplies to term customers would not be affected by the reduction in crude exports.
"Our term clients should not face any problems because of the new Bandar Abbas refinery," he said.
Initial operations at Iran's new 232,000 bpd capacity Bandar Abbas refinery began in June and the plant which runs on Iranian crude is already exporting straight-run fuel oil.
Full capacity is not expected to be reached into late 1998.
Fard said NIOC was not increasing wellhead output to maintain exports as Iranian crude supplies to the new refinery rose.
